findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permissions, disk error)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing filesystem input aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or out-of-range value in sensor data
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV input (empty field, text, overflow) panics instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ...) and propagate through Result, or return a domain ParseError

findings.problem: lossy cast `as u16` after parse silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: valid u32 values (65536..u32::MAX) silently wrap to small u16 values, corrupting sensor data with no error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and propagate the error, or validate range with a checked conversion

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] accessed via unchecked indexing on a Vec without bounds validation
findings.failure_mode: CSV lines with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields (empty lines, trailing newlines, malformed rows) panic with index out of bounds
findings.fix: check parts.len() >= 2 before indexing, or use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) and return a typed error for malformed rows

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) places I/O side effect inside a pure-data parsing function
findings.failure_mode: logging is a hidden side effect that cannot be suppressed in tests, violates pure-core principle, and couples the domain function to console output
findings.fix: remove println! from the parsing pipeline; move any logging to the imperative shell that calls load_sensors, or return a lightweight annotation from the pure function if needed

findings.problem: Collects all split parts into Vec<String> with .collect(), allocating a new String per field per line
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocations and string copies for a line with exactly two fields; memory pressure scales with input size without benefit
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to get exactly two &str parts, then trim and parse without intermediate Vec<String> allocations

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for this I/O-bound data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: no empirical basis to validate performance characteristics or allocation budget for the sensor loading pipeline
findings.fix: add a cargo benchmark or allocation trace (e.g., `mimalloc` stats, `tracing` spans) if performance claims are made

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sensors throughput or allocation profile
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, samply) for the parsing path
no allocation audit (e.g., jemalloc stats, alloc counters) for large-input scaling
no second-ring test or fuzz harness for malformed CSV edge cases
no command evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. Multiple BLOCKERs on unwrap(), lossy as-cast, and unchecked indexing make this crate unacceptable for delivery until all panics are replaced with typed error propagation, the u16 cast is made checked, and indexing is bounds-safe.
